question: Does fine-tuning LMs on agent trajectories (rather than few-shot prompting off-the-shelf LMs) give better, cheaper and more robust language agents, and how do base LM, data size, prompting-method mix and task mix affect this?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning LMs on diverse agent trajectories improves over prompting in performance, efficiency, robustness and generalization.
contributions: Systematic study of language agent fine-tuning across base LMs, prompting methods, data and QA tasks
FireAct: fine-tune LMs on ReAct-format trajectories mixed from multiple tasks and prompting methods (ReAct, CoT, Reflexion)
Findings on scaling, robustness, generalization, efficiency and cost; release of code, data and checkpoints

method.summary: GPT-4 is few-shot prompted (ReAct, CoT, Reflexion) on QA training questions with a Google search tool; only successful (reward = 1) trajectories are kept, reformatted to ReAct format, and used for supervised fine-tuning (distillation) of GPT-3.5, Llama-2 and CodeLlama. Fine-tuned agents run without few-shot prompts.
method.task: open-domain QA agents (thought-action-observation) with a search tool; rejection-sampling-filtered SFT, no RL

datasets.name: HotpotQA
datasets.size: 2,000 random train questions for trajectory curation; 500 random dev questions for evaluation (from 7,405 dev set)
datasets.preprocessing: GPT-4 few-shot trajectories, keep successful ones; 500 ReAct, 187 CoT (single-round ReAct), 47 long Reflexion trajectories (reflection at 6th/10th round) in the multi-method setting; 277 CoT in multi-task setting; human-in-the-loop validation mentioned

datasets.name: StrategyQA
datasets.size: 388 ReAct and 380 CoT trajectories used for multi-task fine-tuning

datasets.name: MMLU
datasets.size: 456 ReAct and 469 CoT trajectories used for multi-task fine-tuning

other.use: generates all fine-tuning data; also prompted baseline (ChatCompletion, Jul-Sep 2023)

training.objective: supervised fine-tuning on successful GPT-4 ReAct-format trajectories (distillation)
training.hardware: LoRA: 1x RTX 4090 24GB (Llama-2-7B/13B, CodeLlama-7B/13B), 1x RTX 6000 Ada 48GB (CodeLlama-34B); full fine-tune Llama-2-7B: 4x A100 80GB
training.compute: LoRA examples/s: Llama-2-7B 5.4, Llama-2-13B 2.5, CodeLlama-7B 5.5, CodeLlama-13B 2.2, CodeLlama-34B 0.9; full FT Llama-2-7B 19.7; about $10 per GPT-3.5 fine-tuning experiment

other.lr_applies_to: B.2 gives one lr 3e-4 without saying which models
other.observation_masking: tested in A.7 (Table 13), no consistent effect

inference.samples: inferred: one run per question; standard errors reported as sigma_M, no multiple seeds stated
inference.prompting: fine-tuned models run with no few-shot examples; prompted baselines use few-shot IO, CoT, ReAct, Reflexion (prompts in Appendix C); ReAct episode hard-limited to 11 steps
inference.retrieval: SerpAPI Google search returning first existent of answer box, answer snippet, highlight words, first result snippet

parameters.reflexion: reflection prompted at 6th and 10th ReAct round
parameters.noisy_tool: probability 0.5 of returning 'None' or a random earlier search response

metrics.name: time and cost per trial
metrics.definition: inference seconds and dollars per trial

baselines: Few-shot IO, CoT, ReAct prompting of GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Llama-2, CodeLlama
eval.protocol: 500 HotpotQA dev questions; standard error sigma_M reported in appendix; no significance test; no multiple seeds stated

prompts.text: Solve a question answering task with interleaving Thought, Action, Observation steps. Thought can reason about the current situation, and Action can be two types: (1) search[question], which searches a question on Google and returns a short snippet containing the answer. Note that sometimes the snippet does not contain the answer, and some alternative search might be needed. (2) finish[answer], which returns the answer and finishes the task. Here are some examples.

evidence.quote: for 3 epochs and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) (Hu et al., 2022) to fine-tune Llama-2 and CodeLlama families for 30 epochs

results.claim: Fine-tuning Llama-2-7B on 500 GPT-4 trajectories raises HotpotQA EM 77% relative over few-shot ReAct.
results.setup: HotpotQA, 500 random dev questions, EM; fine-tuned on 500 successful GPT-4 ReAct trajectories (LoRA for Llama-2/CodeLlama, OpenAI API for GPT-3.5); tool = SerpAPI Google search; Llama-2-7B
results.quote: fine-tuning Llama2-7B with 500 agent trajectories generated by GPT-4 leads to a 77% HotpotQA performance increase

results.claim: Fine-tuned GPT-3.5 (ReAct data) beats few-shot ReAct by 25%.
results.setup: HotpotQA, 500 random dev questions, EM; fine-tuned on 500 successful GPT-4 ReAct trajectories (LoRA for Llama-2/CodeLlama, OpenAI API for GPT-3.5); tool = SerpAPI Google search; GPT-3.5
results.quote: fine-tuning with 500 ReAct trajectories improves the EM to 39.2 (25% increase)

results.claim: Fine-tuning gains: Llama-2-13B 21.2 to 34.4 (+62%), CodeLlama-7B 17.4 to 27.8 (+60%), CodeLlama-13B 20.8 to 29.0 (+39%), CodeLlama-34B 22.2 to 27.8 (+25%); weaker LMs gain more.
results.setup: HotpotQA, 500 random dev questions, EM; fine-tuned on 500 successful GPT-4 ReAct trajectories (LoRA for Llama-2/CodeLlama, OpenAI API for GPT-3.5); tool = SerpAPI Google search; Llama-2-13B
results.quote: While weaker LMs benefit more from fine-tuning (e.g., Llama-2-7B increases by 77%), even strong LMs such as GPT-3.5 could improve performances by 25%

results.claim: Fine-tuned Llama-2-13B outperforms all GPT-3.5 prompting methods (IO 22.4, CoT 28.0, ReAct 31.4).
results.quote: we find fine-tuned Llama-2-13B could outperform all GPT-3.5 prompting methods
results.table: Table 1, GPT-3.5 rows; Table 2, row Llama-2-13B, column FireAct

results.claim: Mixing CoT into ReAct fine-tuning data raises GPT-3.5 HotpotQA EM to 41.0 (31% over prompting).
results.quote: fine-tuning with a mix of ReAct and CoT trajectories further improves the EM to 41.0 (31% increase)
results.table: Table 4, row ReAct + CoT, column EM

results.claim: Fine-tuned GPT-3.5 cuts inference time 70% (9.0s to 2.7s per trial) and cost per trial from 2.6e-3 to 2.2e-3 dollars despite 8x per-token price.
results.setup: GPT-3.5 fine-tuned vs few-shot ReAct, HotpotQA
results.quote: the inference time is reduced by 70% (9.0s to 2.7s per trial)

results.claim: With the search API returning 'None' half the time, ReAct EM falls 33.8% and FireAct only 14.2%.
results.quote: which lowered ReAct EM by 33.8% and FireAct EM only by 14.2%

results.claim: With random observations, ReAct drops 28.0% and FireAct only 5.1%.
results.quote: but does not hurt FireAct much (only 5.1% drop)

results.claim: HotpotQA-fine-tuned GPT-3.5 beats prompted GPT-3.5 on Bamboogle (44.0 vs 40.8 EM).
results.quote: the former (44.0 EM) still beats the latter (40.8 EM)

results.claim: Full fine-tuning of Llama-2-7B gives 30.2 EM vs 26.2 for LoRA (15.3% higher) but needs 4x A100 80GB.
results.quote: full-model fine-tuning (30.2 EM) outperforms LoRA fine-tuning (26.2 EM) by 15.3%

results.claim: GPT-3.5 reaches about 35 EM with 100 samples; Llama models cannot learn the ReAct format with 100 or 200 samples.
results.setup: data scaling n in {100,200,500,1000}, HotpotQA; value read from Fig 3
results.quote: requiring only 100 samples to reach an EM around 35

results.claim: Best mix of methods depends on base LM: ReAct+CoT helps GPT-3.5 and Llama-2 but hurts CodeLlama; ReAct+CoT+Reflexion best for CodeLlama-34B.
results.quote: ReAct+CoT outperforms ReAct for GPT-3.5 and Llama-2 models, but hurts for CodeLlama models.

results.claim: Random method choice gives 32.4 EM, oracle per-instance choice 52.0 EM, versus 39.4 to 41.0 for multi-method agents.
results.table: Table 4, row Oracle method choice, column EM

results.claim: Adding StrategyQA and MMLU data leaves HotpotQA (39.2) and Bamboogle (43.2) about unchanged; multi-task plus CoT improves all tasks (StrategyQA 72.9, Bamboogle 50.4, MMLU 65.8).
All fine-tuned agents and CoT/ReAct prompting underperform IO prompting (68.6) on MMLU.
results.quote: all fine-tuned agents (plus CoT/ReAct prompting) underperform naive input-output (IO) prompting on MMLU

results.claim: CodeLlama tokenizer beats Llama tokenizer: CodeLlama-7B 27.8 vs 26.6, 13B 29.0 vs 27.4.
Observation masking (world-modelling) has no consistent effect on CodeLlama performance.
results.quote: learning world modelling does not have a consistent effect on performance

limits: Single task type (QA) and a single tool (Google search).
Only methods with one autoregressive trajectory context (ReAct, CoT, Reflexion); multi-prompt/multi-role agents not studied.
Multi-task study limited to three QA tasks; best fine-tuned LM is GPT-3.5.
No RL or reward optimisation: reward only filters trajectories.
Single run per setting (no seeds stated); standard errors about 2 EM points so many gaps are within noise.
Optimizer, LoRA rank, sequence length, warmup not stated.
Teacher GPT-4 prompting (CoT 45.0) still beats most fine-tuned students; multi-task MMLU below IO prompting.
Not stated which part of lr/epoch settings applied per model; time-sensitive API models (July-Sept 2023).
